outcome: quality of life (overall, physical, psychological, social relationships, environmental domains)
cohort: The study included 50 women who had experienced a maternal near-miss event between January 1, 2020, and May 31, 2021, during the COVID-19 pandemic.
finding: A maternal near-miss event was not found to adversely affect the overall quality of life or influence contraceptive choices, with no significant difference observed between short-term and long-term QoL.
cross-section timing: Quality of life was assessed at varying points following a maternal near-miss event, which occurred between January 1, 2020, and May 31, 2021.
